column1: # docs/_GOLDENS.tsv - recorded by docs/_gate.sh --record at git tag end-of-44.
# The baseline is a TAG, not a working tree: an uncommitted edit moves these numbers.
# ^ cksum of (size, path) over every .pb the scenes reference. These numbers were measured on
# THOSE bytes, and the gate refuses to compare across a fingerprint change rather than reporting
# an asset swap as a code regression. That is the whole point of the line: a pixel count is only
# Re-armed 2026-09-01 after the P6 re-encode (commit 1f7f4fcb rewrote 10 tracked .pb - mesh_bunny
# -63%, mesh_bunny_grey -61%, floor_model -57% - without updating this line, so the gate had been
# refusing to compare ever since). Re-armed on EVIDENCE, not convenience: the full gate was run
# against the UNCHANGED rows below with the new fingerprint, and every mandatory row matched.
# An earlier version of this comment claimed the re-encoded assets render a different bunny
# (37417 ink, not 44215). That is wrong and was the fake regression it was written during: the
# bunny scene loads mesh_bunny_grey.pb, which IS the re-encoded 4,952,671-byte file today, and it
# renders 44215. The 37417 came from a replay tree whose `ln -sfn` had nested rather than
# replaced, so it was reading the OLD 12,795,331-byte bunny.
